unaccounted-classes.is: the name, the class or the namespace of a prop: it selects the rule that is applied to the prop's value
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: drop, by one decision for all: so the author decided for the one selector of the IFA corpus (the prop name of a response type). What becomes of the value a selector selects is said for that value

unaccounted-classes.is: the `assessment-for` link of an assessment objective (href and rel): the statement the objective assesses
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: carry: `assessment-for` on the objective in sp800-53a@1, as the id of the statement; the CIS Controls converter carries the same link of its source. Where the link names a statement part as a whole there is no statement to name, and a link into another control is to be looked at in the source first

unaccounted-classes.is: the id of a part that gets no id in the bundle: the guidance, an assessment method, a statement part that only groups items, the overview of a family
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: drop: each is the id of its control or family with a fixed suffix (`_gdn`, `_asm-examine`, `_smt`, `_ovw`). To decide together with the `assessment-for` links: the link of a control's first objective names the statement part as a whole, which has no address in the bundle

unaccounted-classes.is: the formal ODP label of a parameter where the converter's round-trip from the parameter id does not give it (parameters of enhancements: `ac-02.01_odp` is labelled `AC-02(01)_ODP`, the rule gives `AC-02.01_ODP`)
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: drop, after the rule is corrected to write the number of the enhancement in brackets: measured on 5.2.0 on 2026-11-14, it then gives 1,455 of the 1,458 labels; or carry the label in odp@1 beside `alt-label`

unaccounted-classes.is: a value carried as a JSON boolean: `contributes-to-assurance` = `true` is written as `true` in rmf@1. The ledger follows strings and integers and cannot see it arrive
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: nothing to decide for the bundle: the value is carried. For the ledger: a way to state a rule whose result is a boolean (oscal_conv_lib), or a declared reason

unaccounted-classes.is: who is responsible for a source document in which role (role-id and party uuid): creator, publisher and their contacts
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: drop with the directory of parties and roles; or carry the publisher as the author in the manifest's provenance, as a landmark URI

unaccounted-classes.is: everything of a withdrawn control that names no successor: its id, title, labels and the one statement that says why it was withdrawn. Nothing of such a control is in the bundle
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: carry: a Requirement with lifecycle `withdrawn` for a control no other control replaces, with its statement as the reason; or drop with that reason stated

unaccounted-classes.is: document metadata the manifest does not hold: `last-modified` of the catalogue and of the four profiles, the `oscal-version` of the profiles, the catalogue's keywords
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: carry: `provenance.source-documents` in the manifest, as the IFA conversion does (title, version, last-modified, oscal-version per document)

unaccounted-classes.is: the catalogue's links to its other forms (`alternate`: the PDF, `canonical`: the DOI, `cprt`: the reference tool)
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: drop: a link to another serialisation of the source, a class decided for IFA; the three resources they name are on the root Set

unaccounted-classes.is: a `related` link to a withdrawn control (href and rel)
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: carry: the relation to the successor the withdrawn control names; or drop, the target being a tombstone

unaccounted-classes.is: the title of the overview part of the PM family
unaccounted-classes.recommendation: carry: beside the overview text in narrative@1; or drop, it repeats the family's title in other words
